# The angle effect

The child sees a target shape and picks which of two shapes is the same
shape rotated. Items are 2-D animals, 2-D polygons and 3-D shapes, each
at several rotation angles. If the task measures mental rotation, items
should get harder as the angle grows.

```{r mrot-items}
mrot_class <- \(uid) case_when(str_detect(uid, "polygon") ~ "2-D polygon",
                               str_detect(uid, "_2d_") ~ "2-D animal",
                               str_detect(uid, "_3d_") ~ "3-D shape")
mrot_items <- items |>
  mutate(stimulus = str_match(item_uid, "mrot_[23]d_([a-z0-9]+)_")[, 2],
         class = mrot_class(item_uid),
         angle = as.integer(str_extract(item_uid, "[0-9]+$")),
         calibration = if_else(n_responses >= min_calib, "well calibrated", "few responses"))
# the angle effect, on items calibrated on enough responses
angle_fit <- lm(difficulty ~ I(angle / 45) * (class == "3-D shape") + stimulus,
                filter(mrot_items, n_responses >= min_calib))
angle_ci <- confint(angle_fit)
slope_2d <- coef(angle_fit)["I(angle/45)"]
slope_3d <- slope_2d + coef(angle_fit)["I(angle/45):class == \"3-D shape\"TRUE"]
thin_mrot <- mrot_items |> filter(n_responses < min_calib)
thin_use <- trials |>
  filter(item_uid %in% thin_mrot$item_uid) |>
  summarise(responses = n(), runs = n_distinct(run_id))
mrot_acc <- trials |>
  mutate(class = mrot_class(item_uid), angle = as.integer(str_extract(item_uid, "[0-9]+$"))) |>
  filter(!is.na(class), !is.na(angle), !is.na(correct)) |>
  group_by(class, angle) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
acc_slope <- mrot_acc |>
  group_by(class) |>
  summarise(lo = accuracy[which.min(angle)], hi = accuracy[which.max(angle)],
            from = min(angle), to = max(angle), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r mrot-angle, fig.height=4.5}
#| label: fig-mrot-angle
#| fig-cap: "Calibrated item difficulty by rotation angle for each stimulus. Open points are items calibrated on fewer than 100 responses."
mrot_items |>
  ggplot(aes(x = angle, y = difficulty, colour = class, group = interaction(stimulus, calibration))) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = calibration), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = calibration), size = 2.2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`well calibrated` = 16, `few responses` = 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`well calibrated` = 1, `few responses` = 3), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`2-D animal` = "#4477AA", `2-D polygon` = "#228833",
                                 `3-D shape` = "#CC6677"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(mrot_items$angle))) +
  labs(x = "Rotation angle (degrees)", y = "Item difficulty")
```

On the items calibrated on `r min_calib` or more responses
(`r paste(sort(unique(filter(mrot_items, n_responses >= min_calib)$stimulus)), collapse = ", ")`),
difficulty rises `r f2(slope_2d)` per 45° of rotation for 2-D items (95% CI
`r f2(angle_ci["I(angle/45)", 1])`–`r f2(angle_ci["I(angle/45)", 2])`) and
`r f2(slope_3d)` per 45° for the 3-D shapes. The other
`r nrow(thin_mrot)` items (`r paste(sort(unique(thin_mrot$stimulus)), collapse = ", ")`)
were calibrated on `r min(thin_mrot$n_responses)`–`r max(thin_mrot$n_responses)`
responses each. Their parameters are poorly determined (discriminations
`r f2(min(thin_mrot$discrimination))`–`r f2(max(thin_mrot$discrimination))`,
close to the model's default of 1) and don't show a consistent angle
effect. They have since been shown
`r fmt_n(thin_use$responses)` times in `r fmt_n(thin_use$runs)` runs.

```{r mrot-acc, fig.height=4}
#| label: fig-mrot-acc
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy by rotation angle and stimulus class; point size shows the number of responses. The dotted line is chance."
mrot_acc |>
  ggplot(aes(x = angle, y = accuracy, colour = class)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = 3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`2-D animal` = "#4477AA", `2-D polygon` = "#228833",
                                 `3-D shape` = "#CC6677"), name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(mrot_acc$angle))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Rotation angle (degrees)", y = "Accuracy")
```

`r with(acc_slope, paste0(class, ": accuracy ", f2(lo), " at ", from, "° and ", f2(hi), " at ", to, "°", collapse = "; "))`.
Because `r fmt_pct(share_adaptive)` of runs are adaptive, accuracy reflects which children saw
which items as well as the items' difficulty; the calibrated difficulties
in @fig-mrot-angle are the cleaner read.

# Open issues

`r below_chance_issue()`
- The goat and polygon items are scored with parameters from a handful of
  responses, though the release now has thousands of responses to them.
  Recalibrating them would put them on a sound footing.
`r poly <- filter(acc_slope, class == "2-D polygon"); if (nrow(poly) == 1 && poly$hi > poly$lo) paste0("- Accuracy on the polygons rises with angle (", f2(poly$lo), " at ", poly$from, "° to ", f2(poly$hi), " at ", poly$to, "°), the reverse of the other stimuli. With the adaptive form this may partly reflect which children saw which items, but the polygon answer keys and rotations are worth checking.") else ""`
- The bank has `r sum(mrot_items$class == "3-D shape")` 3-D items, and
  only `r sum(mrot_items$difficulty > quantile(first_runs$score, .9))` items
  are harder than the top 10% of children's scores (@fig-wright).
